331: 		resolve(selected, project.SectionActiveContractPool, "contract", "contract", true)
332: 	}
333: 	for _, selected := range idx.ReviewProtocols {
334: 		resolve(selected, project.SectionReviewProtocols, "protocol", "protocol", false)
335: 	}
336: 	if unresolvedExecutePlanTasks(manifest.Contents[ArtifactRelPath(sp, StagePlan)], runContent, planManifest) {
337: 		findings = append(findings, finding("Plan Execution", "tasks", ArtifactRelPath(sp, StagePlan), "plan tasks are not resolved", "one or more unchecked top-level tasks lack an explicit deferred run-state outcome", "Complete each executable task or defer it with an explicit rationale before review."))
338: 	}
339: 	// The handbook receives an independent reviewer even though it is also a governed input.
340: 	if handbook := findReviewInput(manifest.Inputs, "technical-handbook"); handbook.Path != "" {
341: 		handbook.ID, handbook.Kind, handbook.Name = "handbook", "handbook", "Technical Handbook"
342: 		manifest.Coverage = append(manifest.Coverage, handbook)
343: 	}
344: 	if strings.TrimSpace(manifest.Model) == "" || manifest.Model == "unresolved" {
345: 		findings = append(findings, finding("Configuration", "review model", "", "missing review model", "no review, plan, or runtime model is configured", "Set planning.review_model or planning.plan_model."))
346: 	}
347: 	for _, command := range reviewVerificationCommands(manifest.Contents[ArtifactRelPath(sp, StagePlan)]) {
348: 		if !strings.Contains(manifest.Contents[ArtifactRelPath(sp, StageExecute)], command) {
349: 			findings = append(findings, finding("Verification Evidence", command, ArtifactRelPath(sp, StageExecute), "approved verification evidence missing", "execute.md does not record the planned command", "Run the approved command and record its result in execute.md."))
350: 		}
351: 	}
352: 	if runContent != "" && reviewRunStateIncomplete([]byte(runContent)) {
353: 		findings = append(findings, finding("Plan Execution", "run-state", runPath, "execute is incomplete", "run state contains non-complete tasks or status", "Complete or safely resolve execute before review."))
354: 	}
355: 	if len(manifest.ChangedPaths) == 0 {
356: 		manifest.ChangedPaths = []string{"(execute evidence did not enumerate changed paths)"}
357: 	} else {
358: 		for _, changed := range manifest.ChangedPaths {
359: 			full := changed
360: 			if !filepath.IsAbs(full) {
361: 				full = filepath.Join(manifest.Target, filepath.FromSlash(changed))
362: 			}
363: 			if !inside(manifest.Target, full) {
364: 				findings = append(findings, finding("Review target", changed, changed, "changed path escapes target", "path is outside the approved implementation target", "Use contained execute evidence."))
365: 				continue
366: 			}
367: 			data, readErr := os.ReadFile(full)
368: 			if readErr != nil {
369: 				findings = append(findings, finding("Review target", changed, changed, "changed target input unreadable", readErr.Error(), "Restore the changed path or correct execute evidence."))
370: 				continue
371: 			}
372: 			rel, _ := filepath.Rel(manifest.Target, full)
373: 			manifest.Inputs = append(manifest.Inputs, reviewInput("target-"+slugReviewID(rel), "target", rel, "target/"+filepath.ToSlash(rel), string(data)))
374: 			manifest.Contents["target/"+filepath.ToSlash(rel)] = string(data)
375: 		}
376: 	}
377: 	if patch, available, patchErr := buildReviewPatch(sp, manifest.Target, manifest.ChangedPaths); patchErr != nil {
378: 		findings = append(findings, finding("Review target", "implementation diff", reviewPatchPath, "cannot create baseline-to-sprint review patch", patchErr.Error(), "Restore the sprint worktree and its recorded baseline before review."))
379: 	} else if available {
380: 		manifest.Inputs = append(manifest.Inputs, reviewInput("implementation-diff", "implementation-diff", "baseline-to-sprint patch", reviewPatchPath, patch))
381: 		manifest.Contents[reviewPatchPath] = patch
382: 	}
383: 	sort.Slice(manifest.Coverage, func(i, j int) bool { return manifest.Coverage[i].ID < manifest.Coverage[j].ID })
384: 	sort.Slice(manifest.Inputs, func(i, j int) bool { return manifest.Inputs[i].Path < manifest.Inputs[j].Path })
385: 	manifest.Fingerprint = fingerprintReviewManifest(manifest)
386: 	sortSprintFindings(findings)
387: 	return manifest, findings, nil
388: }

418: func (s Service) Review(ctx context.Context, projectRef, sprintRef string, req ReviewRequest) (ReviewResult, error) {
419: 	m, findings, err := s.PrepareReview(projectRef, sprintRef, req)
420: 	result := ReviewResult{Project: m.Project, Sprint: m.Sprint, DryRun: req.DryRun, Fingerprint: m.Fingerprint, Artifact: reviewArtifact(m), Status: ReviewReady, Focused: append([]string(nil), req.Focus...)}
421: 	if err != nil {
422: 		return result, err
423: 	}
424: 	if !req.DryRun && !req.PromptOnly {
425: 		lockedCtx, release, lockErr := s.acquireMutationContext(ctx, projectRef, sprintRef)
426: 		if lockErr != nil {
427: 			return result, lockErr
428: 		}
429: 		defer release()
430: 		ctx = lockedCtx
431: 	}
432: 	if len(findings) > 0 {
433: 		result.Status, result.Verdict = ReviewBlocked, ReviewVerdictBlocked
434: 		for _, f := range findings {
435: 			result.Diagnostics = append(result.Diagnostics, ReviewDiagnostic{Code: "preflight", Message: safeReviewText(s.root, f.Problem+": "+f.Cause)})
436: 		}
437: 		if !req.DryRun {
438: 			if saveErr := s.saveReviewState(projectRef, sprintRef, result, 0, len(m.Coverage)); saveErr != nil {
439: 				return result, errors.Join(fmt.Errorf("review prerequisites failed validation"), saveErr)
440: 			}
441: 		}
442: 		return result, fmt.Errorf("review prerequisites failed validation")
443: 	}
444: 	sp, inputs, _, err := s.resolveSprintInputs(projectRef, sprintRef)
445: 	if err != nil {
446: 		return result, err
447: 	}
448: 	m.SharedPrefix, err = s.prepareSharedPromptContext(ctx, sp, inputs, true)
449: 	if err != nil {
450: 		if errors.Is(err, context.Canceled) || errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded) {
451: 			result.Status = ReviewCancelled
452: 			result.Diagnostics = append(result.Diagnostics, ReviewDiagnostic{Code: "cancelled", Message: safeReviewText(s.root, err.Error())})
453: 			if !req.DryRun && !req.PromptOnly {
454: 				return s.persistReviewFailure(projectRef, sprintRef, result, 0, len(m.Coverage), err)
455: 			}
456: 		}
457: 		return result, err
458: 	}
459: 	result.Prompt, err = composeStagePromptChecked(m.SharedPrefix, renderReviewPreview(m))
460: 	if err != nil {
461: 		return result, err
462: 	}
463: 	if req.DryRun || req.PromptOnly {
464: 		result.Message = "review dry run"
465: 		return result, nil
466: 	}
467: 	if s.runtime == nil {
468: 		return result, fmt.Errorf("runtime is required for review")
469: 	}
470: 	if req.Restart && len(req.Focus) > 0 {
471: 		return result, fmt.Errorf("--restart cannot be combined with focused review")
472: 	}
473: 	result.Status = ReviewRunning
474: 	result.Restarted = req.Restart
475: 	if err := s.saveReviewState(projectRef, sprintRef, result, 0, len(m.Coverage)); err != nil {
476: 		return result, err
477: 	}
478: 	runCoverage, coverage, focusErr := s.reviewCoveragePlan(projectRef, sprintRef, m, req.Focus)
479: 	if focusErr != nil {
480: 		result.Status, result.Verdict = ReviewBlocked, ReviewVerdictBlocked
481: 		result.Diagnostics = append(result.Diagnostics, ReviewDiagnostic{Code: "focus", Message: safeReviewText(s.root, focusErr.Error())})
482: 		return s.persistReviewFailure(projectRef, sprintRef, result, 0, len(m.Coverage), focusErr)
483: 	}
484: 	resumeSessions := map[string]string{}
485: 	completed := 0
486: 	if len(req.Focus) == 0 {
487: 		resume, rebased, resumeErr := s.initializeReviewResume(projectRef, sprintRef, m, req.Restart)
488: 		if resumeErr != nil {
489: 			result.Status, result.Verdict = ReviewFailed, ReviewVerdictBlocked
490: 			result.Diagnostics = append(result.Diagnostics, ReviewDiagnostic{Code: "resume-state", Message: safeReviewText(s.root, resumeErr.Error())})
491: 			return s.persistReviewFailure(projectRef, sprintRef, result, 0, len(m.Coverage), resumeErr)
492: 		}
493: 		runCoverage, coverage, resumeSessions, completed = reviewResumePlan(s.root, m, resume)
494: 		result.Resumed = !req.Restart && (completed > 0 || len(resumeSessions) > 0)
495: 		result.Reused = completed
496: 		if rebased > 0 {
497: 			result.Diagnostics = append(result.Diagnostics, ReviewDiagnostic{Code: "resume-rebased", Message: fmt.Sprintf("reused %d validated reviewer result(s) from the prior input fingerprint; incomplete coverage uses the current snapshot", rebased)})
498: 		}
499: 	}
500: 	reviewerRoot, snapshotErr := prepareReviewSnapshot(m)
501: 	if snapshotErr != nil {
502: 		result.Status, result.Verdict = ReviewFailed, ReviewVerdictBlocked
503: 		result.Diagnostics = append(result.Diagnostics, ReviewDiagnostic{Code: "snapshot", Message: safeReviewText(s.root, snapshotErr.Error())})
504: 		if saveErr := s.saveReviewState(projectRef, sprintRef, result, 0, len(m.Coverage)); saveErr != nil {
505: 			return result, errors.Join(snapshotErr, saveErr)
506: 		}
507: 		return result, snapshotErr
508: 	}
509: 	m.ReviewerRoot = reviewerRoot
510: 	workers := m.Concurrency
511: 	if workers > len(runCoverage) {
512: 		workers = len(runCoverage)
513: 	}
514: 	if workers < 1 {
515: 		workers = 1
516: 	}
517: 	type item struct {
518: 		index     int
519: 		value     ReviewCoverageResult
520: 		sessionID string
521: 	}
522: 	type sessionItem struct {
523: 		coverageID string
524: 		sessionID  string
525: 	}
526: 	jobs := make(chan int)
527: 	done := make(chan item, len(runCoverage))
528: 	sessions := make(chan sessionItem, max(1, len(runCoverage)*4))
529: 	var wg sync.WaitGroup
530: 	for w := 0; w < workers; w++ {
531: 		wg.Add(1)
532: 		go func() {
533: 			defer wg.Done()
534: 			for i := range jobs {
535: 				c := runCoverage[i]
536: 				sessionID := resumeSessions[c.ID]
537: 				lastSessionID := sessionID
538: 				value, finalSessionID := s.runReviewer(ctx, m, c, sessionID, func(id string) {
539: 					if id != "" && id != lastSessionID {
540: 						lastSessionID = id
541: 						sessions <- sessionItem{coverageID: c.ID, sessionID: id}
542: 					}
543: 				})
544: 				done <- item{index: i, value: value, sessionID: finalSessionID}
545: 			}
546: 		}()
547: 	}
548: 	go func() {
549: 		for i := range runCoverage {
550: 			jobs <- i
551: 		}
552: 		close(jobs)
553: 		wg.Wait()
554: 		close(sessions)
555: 		close(done)
556: 	}()
557: 	var progressSaveErr error
558: 	completedSessionIDs := map[string]bool{}
559: 	for done != nil || sessions != nil {
560: 		select {
561: 		case session, ok := <-sessions:
562: 			if !ok {
563: 				sessions = nil
564: 				continue
565: 			}
566: 			if session.sessionID != "" && len(req.Focus) == 0 {
567: 				if saveErr := s.saveReviewResumeSession(projectRef, sprintRef, m.Fingerprint, session.coverageID, session.sessionID); saveErr != nil {
568: 					progressSaveErr = errors.Join(progressSaveErr, saveErr)
569: 				}
570: 			}
571: 		case got, ok := <-done:
572: 			if !ok {
573: 				done = nil
574: 				continue
575: 			}
576: 			if got.value.Error == "" && !reviewCoverageCheckpointValid(s.root, m, got.value) {
577: 				got.value.Error = "reviewer result failed schema or citation validation"
578: 			}
579: 			for i := range m.Coverage {
580: 				if m.Coverage[i].ID == got.value.CoverageID {
581: 					coverage[i] = got.value
582: 					break
583: 				}
584: 			}
585: 			completed++
586: 			if got.sessionID != "" {
587: 				completedSessionIDs[got.sessionID] = true
588: 			}
589: 			if req.Progress != nil {
590: 				req.Progress(ReviewProgress{Completed: completed, Total: len(coverage), CoverageID: got.value.CoverageID, Message: "reviewer complete"})
591: 			}
592: 			result.Coverage = coverage
593: 			if len(req.Focus) == 0 {
594: 				if saveErr := s.saveReviewResumeResult(projectRef, sprintRef, m.Fingerprint, got.value, got.sessionID); saveErr != nil {
595: 					progressSaveErr = errors.Join(progressSaveErr, saveErr)
596: 				}
597: 			}
598: 			if saveErr := s.saveReviewState(projectRef, sprintRef, result, completed, len(coverage)); saveErr != nil {
599: 				progressSaveErr = errors.Join(progressSaveErr, saveErr)
600: 			}
601: 		}
602: 	}
603: 	result.Coverage = coverage
604: 	validatedFindings, validationDiagnostics, validatedVerdict := validateReviewCoverage(s.root, m, coverage)
605: 	result.Findings = validatedFindings
606: 	result.Diagnostics = append(result.Diagnostics, validationDiagnostics...)
607: 	result.Verdict = validatedVerdict
608: 	if progressSaveErr != nil {
609: 		result.Status, result.Verdict = ReviewFailed, ReviewVerdictBlocked
610: 		result.Diagnostics = append(result.Diagnostics, ReviewDiagnostic{Code: "state-write-failed", Message: safeReviewText(s.root, progressSaveErr.Error())})
611: 		return s.persistReviewFailure(projectRef, sprintRef, result, completed, len(coverage), progressSaveErr)
612: 	}
613: 	if ctx.Err() != nil {
614: 		result.Status = ReviewCancelled
615: 		result.Diagnostics = append(result.Diagnostics, ReviewDiagnostic{Code: "cancelled", Message: ctx.Err().Error()})
616: 		return s.persistReviewFailure(projectRef, sprintRef, result, completed, len(coverage), ctx.Err())
617: 	}
618: 	if result.Verdict == ReviewVerdictBlocked {
619: 		result.Status = ReviewFailed
620: 		return s.persistReviewFailure(projectRef, sprintRef, result, completed, len(coverage), fmt.Errorf("review failed to produce complete valid coverage"))
621: 	}
622: 	current, currentFindings, currentErr := s.PrepareReview(projectRef, sprintRef, req)
623: 	if currentErr != nil || len(currentFindings) > 0 || current.Fingerprint != m.Fingerprint {
624: 		for _, message := range reviewManifestChanges(m, current, currentFindings, currentErr) {
625: 			result.Diagnostics = append(result.Diagnostics, ReviewDiagnostic{Code: "inputs-changed", Message: safeReviewText(s.root, message)})
626: 		}
627: 	}
628: 	result.Status = ReviewCompleted
629: 	content := RenderReviewMarkdown(m, result)
630: 	if vf := ValidateReviewContent(content, m); len(vf) > 0 {
631: 		result.Status = ReviewFailed
632: 		result.Diagnostics = append(result.Diagnostics, ReviewDiagnostic{Code: "artifact-invalid", Message: vf[0].Problem})
633: 		return s.persistReviewFailure(projectRef, sprintRef, result, completed, len(coverage), fmt.Errorf("generated review.md failed validation"))
634: 	}
635: 	path, _ := ArtifactPath(s.root, sp, StageReview)
636: 	if err := atomicWriteReview(path, []byte(content)); err != nil {
637: 		result.Status = ReviewFailed
638: 		result.Diagnostics = append(result.Diagnostics, ReviewDiagnostic{Code: "write-failed", Message: safeError(err)})
639: 		return s.persistReviewFailure(projectRef, sprintRef, result, completed, len(coverage), err)
640: 	}
641: 	now := s.now().UTC()
642: 	result.Message = "review complete"
643: 	result.Artifact = ArtifactRelPath(sp, StageReview)
644: 	if err := s.saveReviewState(projectRef, sprintRef, result, completed, len(coverage)); err != nil {
645: 		return result, err
646: 	}
647: 	publications, publishErr := s.publishReviewStage(ctx, sp)
648: 	result.Publications = append(result.Publications, publications...)
649: 	if publishErr != nil {
650: 		return result, publishErr
651: 	}
652: 	_ = os.RemoveAll(reviewerRoot)
653: 	_ = now
654: 	if result.Verdict == ReviewFail {
655: 		return result, fmt.Errorf("review completed with failing verdict")
656: 	}
657: 	for sessionID := range completedSessionIDs {
658: 		_ = s.deleteCompletedSession(ctx, sessionID)
659: 	}
660: 	return result, nil
661: }

665: 		return result, errors.Join(cause, fmt.Errorf("persist terminal review state: %w", saveErr))
666: 	}
667: 	return result, cause

670: func (s Service) reviewCoveragePlan(projectRef, sprintRef string, m ReviewManifest, focus []string) ([]ReviewInput, []ReviewCoverageResult, error) {
671: 	coverage := make([]ReviewCoverageResult, len(m.Coverage))
672: 	if len(focus) == 0 {
673: 		return m.Coverage, coverage, nil
674: 	}
675: 	wanted := map[string]bool{}
676: 	for _, raw := range focus {
677: 		for _, id := range strings.Split(raw, ",") {
678: 			id = strings.TrimSpace(id)
679: 			if id != "" {
680: 				wanted[id] = true
681: 			}
682: 		}
683: 	}
684: 	state, err := LoadFlowState(s.root, Sprint{Project: m.Project, Slug: m.Sprint, Path: filepath.Join(s.root, filepath.FromSlash(m.SprintRoot))})
685: 	if err != nil || state.Review == nil || state.Review.LastComplete == nil {
686: 		return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("focused review requires a previous complete review with retained coverage")
687: 	}
688: 	previous := state.Review.LastComplete
689: 	if previous.InputFingerprint != m.Fingerprint {
690: 		return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("focused review cannot retain coverage from a different input fingerprint")
691: 	}
692: 	retained := map[string]ReviewCoverageResult{}
693: 	for _, item := range previous.Coverage {
694: 		retained[item.CoverageID] = item
695: 	}
696: 	var run []ReviewInput
697: 	for i, item := range m.Coverage {
698: 		if wanted[item.ID] {
699: 			run = append(run, item)
700: 			delete(wanted, item.ID)
701: 			continue
702: 		}
703: 		prior, ok := retained[item.ID]
704: 		if !ok || prior.Error != "" {
705: 			return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("focused review lacks valid retained coverage %q", item.ID)
706: 		}
707: 		coverage[i] = prior
708: 	}
709: 	if len(wanted) > 0 {
710: 		return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("focused review names unknown coverage")
711: 	}
712: 	if len(run) == 0 {
713: 		return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("focused review requires at least one coverage id")
714: 	}
715: 	return run, coverage, nil
716: }

718: func (s Service) initializeReviewResume(projectRef, sprintRef string, m ReviewManifest, restart bool) (ReviewResumeState, int, error) {
719: 	sp, _, _, err := s.resolveSprintInputs(projectRef, sprintRef)
720: 	if err != nil {
721: 		return ReviewResumeState{}, 0, err
722: 	}
723: 	state, err := LoadFlowState(s.root, sp)
724: 	if err != nil {
725: 		return ReviewResumeState{}, 0, err
726: 	}
727: 	if state.Review == nil || state.Review.ActiveAttempt == nil {
728: 		return ReviewResumeState{}, 0, fmt.Errorf("review attempt state is unavailable")
729: 	}
730: 	current := state.Review.Resume
731: 	rebased := 0
732: 	if restart || !reviewResumeCompatible(current, m) {
733: 		checkpoints := make([]ReviewCoverageCheckpoint, 0, len(m.Coverage))
734: 		now := s.now().UTC()
735: 		prior := map[string]ReviewCoverageCheckpoint{}
736: 		if !restart && reviewResumeShapeCompatible(current, m) {
737: 			for _, checkpoint := range current.Coverage {
738: 				prior[checkpoint.CoverageID] = checkpoint
739: 			}
740: 		}
741: 		for _, item := range m.Coverage {
742: 			checkpoint := ReviewCoverageCheckpoint{CoverageID: item.ID, Status: AttemptPending, UpdatedAt: now}
743: 			if previous, ok := prior[item.ID]; ok && previous.Status == AttemptCompleted && previous.Result != nil && reviewCoverageCheckpointValid(s.root, m, *previous.Result) {
744: 				checkpoint.Status = AttemptCompleted
745: 				checkpoint.Result = previous.Result
746: 				rebased++
747: 			}
748: 			checkpoints = append(checkpoints, checkpoint)
749: 		}
750: 		current = &ReviewResumeState{
751: 			AttemptID:        state.Review.ActiveAttempt.ID,
752: 			InputFingerprint: m.Fingerprint,
753: 			Model:            m.Model,
754: 			UpdatedAt:        now,
755: 			Coverage:         checkpoints,
756: 		}
757: 	} else {
758: 		current.AttemptID = state.Review.ActiveAttempt.ID
759: 		current.UpdatedAt = s.now().UTC()
760: 	}
761: 	state.Review.Resume = current
762: 	if err := SaveFlowState(s.root, sp, state); err != nil {
763: 		return ReviewResumeState{}, 0, err
764: 	}
765: 	return *current, rebased, nil
766: }
767: 
768: func reviewResumeCompatible(state *ReviewResumeState, m ReviewManifest) bool {
769: 	return state != nil && state.InputFingerprint == m.Fingerprint && reviewResumeShapeCompatible(state, m)
770: }
771: 
772: func reviewResumeShapeCompatible(state *ReviewResumeState, m ReviewManifest) bool {
773: 	if state == nil || state.Model != m.Model || len(state.Coverage) != len(m.Coverage) {
774: 		return false
775: 	}
776: 	seen := map[string]bool{}
777: 	for _, item := range state.Coverage {
778: 		seen[item.CoverageID] = true
779: 	}
780: 	for _, item := range m.Coverage {
781: 		if !seen[item.ID] {
782: 			return false
783: 		}
784: 	}
785: 	return true
786: }

788: func reviewResumePlan(root string, m ReviewManifest, state ReviewResumeState) ([]ReviewInput, []ReviewCoverageResult, map[string]string, int) {
789: 	checkpoints := map[string]ReviewCoverageCheckpoint{}
790: 	for _, item := range state.Coverage {
791: 		checkpoints[item.CoverageID] = item
792: 	}
793: 	coverage := make([]ReviewCoverageResult, len(m.Coverage))
794: 	sessions := map[string]string{}

1237: 	if r.Restarted && r.Status == ReviewRunning && completed == 0 && len(r.Coverage) == 0 {
1238: 		current.ActiveAttempt = nil
1239: 		current.Resume = nil
1240: 	}
1241: 	if len(r.Focused) > 0 && r.Status == ReviewRunning && completed == 0 && len(r.Coverage) == 0 {
1242: 		current.ActiveAttempt = nil
1243: 		current.Resume = nil
1244: 	}
1245: 	current.Status, current.LastRunAt, current.Completed, current.Total, current.Diagnostics = r.Status, &now, completed, total, append([]ReviewDiagnostic(nil), r.Diagnostics...)
1246: 	current.ProvisionalVerdict = r.ProvisionalVerdict
1247: 	attempt := VerificationAttempt{ID: fmt.Sprintf("review-%d", now.UnixNano()), Status: AttemptRunning, StartedAt: now, HeartbeatAt: now, OwnerPID: os.Getpid()}
1248: 	if current.ActiveAttempt != nil {
1249: 		attempt = *current.ActiveAttempt
1250: 	}
1251: 	if r.Status == ReviewRunning {
1252: 		attempt.HeartbeatAt = now
1253: 		attempt.OwnerPID = os.Getpid()
1254: 		current.ActiveAttempt = &attempt
1255: 		if current.Resume != nil && !r.Restarted {
1256: 			current.Resume.AttemptID = attempt.ID
1257: 		}
1258: 	} else {
1259: 		attempt.CompletedAt = &now
1260: 		attempt.Diagnostics = reviewDiagnosticStrings(r.Diagnostics)
1261: 		attempt.Status = reviewAttemptStatus(r.Status)
1262: 		current.ActiveAttempt, current.LastAttempt = nil, &attempt
1263: 	}
1264: 	if r.Status == ReviewCompleted {
1265: 		current.ProvisionalVerdict = ""
1266: 		digest, _ := hashFile(mustArtifactPath(s.root, sp, StageReview))
1267: 		current.Verdict, current.Fingerprint, current.ArtifactDigest, current.Stale = r.Verdict, r.Fingerprint, digest, false
1268: 		current.LastComplete = &ReviewCompletion{Verdict: r.Verdict, Artifact: ArtifactRelPath(sp, StageReview), ArtifactDigest: digest, InputFingerprint: r.Fingerprint, CompletedAt: now, Coverage: append([]ReviewCoverageResult(nil), r.Coverage...)}
1269: 		current.Resume = nil
1270: 	} else if current.LastComplete != nil {
1271: 		current.Verdict, current.Fingerprint, current.ArtifactDigest = current.LastComplete.Verdict, current.LastComplete.InputFingerprint, current.LastComplete.ArtifactDigest
1272: 	} else {
1273: 		current.Verdict, current.Fingerprint = r.Verdict, r.Fingerprint
1274: 	}
1275: 	state.Review = current
1276: 	return SaveFlowState(s.root, sp, state)
1277: }

1604: func prepareReviewSnapshot(m ReviewManifest) (string, error) {
1605: 	if m.Fingerprint == "" || strings.ContainsAny(m.Fingerprint, "\\/\x00\r\n") {
1606: 		return "", fmt.Errorf("create frozen review snapshot: invalid fingerprint")
1607: 	}
1608: 	root := filepath.Join(m.WorkspaceRoot, ".ultra", "cache", "review", m.Project, m.Sprint, m.Fingerprint)
1609: 	marker := filepath.Join(root, ".complete")
1610: 	if _, err := os.Stat(marker); err == nil {
1611: 		return root, nil
1612: 	}
1613: 	if err := os.RemoveAll(root); err != nil {
1614: 		return "", fmt.Errorf("reset incomplete frozen review snapshot: %w", err)
1615: 	}
1616: 	if err := os.MkdirAll(root, 0o700); err != nil {
1617: 		return "", fmt.Errorf("create frozen review snapshot: %w", err)
1618: 	}
1619: 	cleanup := true
1620: 	defer func() {
1621: 		if cleanup {
1622: 			_ = os.RemoveAll(root)
1623: 		}
1624: 	}()
1625: 	for _, in := range m.Inputs {
1626: 		if in.Kind == "asset" || in.Path == "target/.identity" {
1627: 			continue
1628: 		}
1629: 		content, ok := m.Contents[in.Path]
1630: 		if !ok {
1631: 			return "", fmt.Errorf("frozen review input %q has no captured content", in.Path)
1632: 		}
1633: 		copyManifest := m
1634: 		copyManifest.ReviewerRoot = root
1635: 		path := reviewInputReadPath(copyManifest, in)
1636: 		if !inside(root, path) {
1637: 			return "", fmt.Errorf("frozen review input %q escapes snapshot", in.Path)
1638: 		}
1639: 		if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(path), 0o700); err != nil {
1640: 			return "", fmt.Errorf("create frozen review snapshot directory: %w", err)
1641: 		}
1642: 		if err := os.WriteFile(path, []byte(content), 0o400); err != nil {
1643: 			return "", fmt.Errorf("write frozen review input %q: %w", in.Path, err)
1644: 		}
1645: 	}
1646: 	if err := os.WriteFile(marker, []byte(m.Fingerprint+"\n"), 0o400); err != nil {
1647: 		return "", fmt.Errorf("complete frozen review snapshot: %w", err)
1648: 	}
1649: 	cleanup = false
1650: 	return root, nil
1651: }
1652: func extractReviewResult(r pruntime.Result, out *ReviewCoverageResult) bool {
1653: 	if extractReviewValue(r.TerminalOutput, out) {
1654: 		return true
1655: 	}
1656: 	for i := len(r.Events) - 1; i >= 0; i-- {
1657: 		if extractReviewValue(r.Events[i].Payload, out) {
1658: 			return true
1659: 		}
1660: 	}
1661: 	return false
1662: }
1663: func extractReviewValue(v any, out *ReviewCoverageResult) bool {
1664: 	switch x := v.(type) {
1665: 	case map[string]any:
1666: 		var candidate ReviewCoverageResult
1667: 		if raw, e := json.Marshal(x); e == nil && json.Unmarshal(raw, &candidate) == nil && candidate.CoverageID != "" {
1668: 			*out = candidate
1669: 			return true
1670: 		}
1671: 		for _, k := range []string{"review_result", "structured_output", "output", "content", "text", "message", "part"} {
1672: 			if y, ok := x[k]; ok && extractReviewValue(y, out) {
1673: 				return true
1674: 			}
1675: 		}
1676: 	case []any:
1677: 		for i := len(x) - 1; i >= 0; i-- {
1678: 			if extractReviewValue(x[i], out) {
1679: 				return true
1680: 			}
1681: 		}
1682: 	case string:
1683: 		return extractReviewJSON(x, out)
1684: 	}
1685: 	return false
1686: }
1687: 
1688: // extractReviewJSON tolerates runtime output that contains reasoning, Markdown,
1689: // or other prose before the canonical result. Trying each object boundary with
1690: // a streaming decoder avoids the brittle first-"{"/last-"}" assumption while
1691: // still accepting only an object that decodes as an actual review result.
1692: func extractReviewJSON(value string, out *ReviewCoverageResult) bool {
1693: 	found := false
1694: 	for offset := 0; offset < len(value); {
1695: 		relative := strings.IndexByte(value[offset:], '{')
1696: 		if relative < 0 {
1697: 			break
1698: 		}
1699: 		start := offset + relative
1700: 		var candidate ReviewCoverageResult
1701: 		if err := json.NewDecoder(strings.NewReader(value[start:])).Decode(&candidate); err == nil && candidate.CoverageID != "" {
1702: 			*out = candidate
1703: 			found = true
1704: 		}
1705: 		offset = start + 1
1706: 	}
1707: 	return found
1708: }

1714: 	if !ok {

310: func (a Adapter) StartRun(ctx context.Context, req Request) (Result, error) {
311: 	if a.runtime == nil {
312: 		return Result{}, fmt.Errorf("runtime is required")
313: 	}
314: 	if req.RuntimeStorePath != "" {
315: 		if err := prepareRuntimeStore(req.RuntimeStorePath, req.RuntimeStoreOwner); err != nil {
316: 			return Result{RuntimeStorePath: req.RuntimeStorePath}, err
317: 		}
318: 	}
319: 	awReq, err := toAgentwrapRequest(req)
320: 	if err != nil {
321: 		retainRuntimeStore(req.RuntimeStorePath, req.RuntimeStoreOwner, err)
322: 		return Result{RuntimeStorePath: req.RuntimeStorePath}, err
323: 	}
324: 	run, err := a.runtime.StartRun(ctx, awReq)
325: 	if err != nil {
326: 		mappedErr := mapError(err)
327: 		retainRuntimeStore(req.RuntimeStorePath, req.RuntimeStoreOwner, mappedErr)
328: 		return Result{RuntimeStorePath: req.RuntimeStorePath}, mappedErr
329: 	}
330: 
331: 	eventsCh := make(chan eventCollection, 1)
332: 	go func() {
333: 		events := newEventCollection(retainedRuntimeEventLimit)
334: 		for event := range run.Events() {
335: 			events.captureTerminalOutput(event.Payload)
336: 			mapped := mapEvent(event)
337: 			events.add(mapped)
338: 			if req.OnEvent != nil {
339: 				req.OnEvent(mapped)
340: 			}
341: 		}
342: 		events.finish()
343: 		eventsCh <- events
344: 	}()
345: 
346: 	type waitResult struct {
347: 		result agentwrap.RunResult
348: 		err    error
349: 	}
350: 	waitCh := make(chan waitResult, 1)
351: 	go func() {
352: 		result, err := run.Wait(ctx)
353: 		waitCh <- waitResult{result: result, err: err}
354: 	}()
355: 
356: 	var result agentwrap.RunResult
357: 	var waitErr error
358: 	select {
359: 	case waited := <-waitCh:
360: 		result = waited.result
361: 		waitErr = waited.err
362: 	case <-ctx.Done():
363: 		_ = run.Cancel(context.Background())
364: 		select {
365: 		case waited := <-waitCh:
366: 			result = waited.result
367: 			waitErr = waited.err
368: 		case <-time.After(5 * time.Second):
369: 			mapped := Result{
370: 				Status:           "cancelled",
371: 				FinishedAt:       time.Now(),
372: 				Error:            &Error{Category: "cancellation", Operation: "run", UserDetail: ctx.Err().Error()},
373: 				RuntimeStorePath: req.RuntimeStorePath,
374: 			}
375: 			retainRuntimeStore(req.RuntimeStorePath, req.RuntimeStoreOwner, ctx.Err())
376: 			return mapped, ctx.Err()
377: 		}
378: 		if waitErr == nil {
379: 			waitErr = ctx.Err()
380: 		}
381: 	}
382: 
383: 	mapped := mapResult(result)
384: 	mapped.RuntimeStorePath = req.RuntimeStorePath
385: 	select {
386: 	case events := <-eventsCh:
387: 		mapped.Events = events.events
388: 		if mapped.TerminalOutput == "" && events.terminalOutput != "" {
389: 			mapped.TerminalOutput = events.terminalOutput
390: 		}
391: 		mapped.EventStats = events.stats()
392: 		mapped.Memory = events.memory
393: 		mapped.SessionIDs = append([]string(nil), events.sessionIDs...)
394: 		if mapped.SessionID != "" && !events.seenSessions[mapped.SessionID] {
395: 			mapped.SessionIDs = append(mapped.SessionIDs, mapped.SessionID)
396: 		}
397: 		if events.dropped > 0 {
398: 			mapped.Warnings = append(mapped.Warnings, fmt.Sprintf("runtime retained last %d events and dropped %d earlier events from in-memory result", events.limit, events.dropped))
399: 		}
400: 	case <-time.After(time.Second):
401: 	}
402: 	if waitErr != nil {
403: 		retainRuntimeStore(req.RuntimeStorePath, req.RuntimeStoreOwner, waitErr)
404: 		if errors.Is(waitErr, context.Canceled) {
405: 			mapped.Status = "cancelled"
406: 			mapped.Error = &Error{Category: "cancellation", Operation: "run", UserDetail: waitErr.Error()}
407: 		} else if errors.Is(waitErr, context.DeadlineExceeded) {
408: 			mapped.Status = "failed"
409: 			mapped.Error = &Error{Category: "timeout", Operation: "run", UserDetail: waitErr.Error()}
410: 		}
411: 		return mapped, mapError(waitErr)
412: 	}
413: 	if result.Err != nil {
414: 		retainRuntimeStore(req.RuntimeStorePath, req.RuntimeStoreOwner, result.Err)
415: 		return mapped, mapError(result.Err)
416: 	}
417: 	retainRuntimeStore(req.RuntimeStorePath, req.RuntimeStoreOwner, nil)
418: 	return mapped, nil
419: }

421: type eventCollection struct {
422: 	events         []Event
423: 	terminalOutput string
424: 	total          int64
425: 	dropped        int64
426: 	limit          int
427: 	memory         MemoryStats
428: 	sessionIDs     []string
429: 	seenSessions   map[string]bool
430: }
431: 
432: func newEventCollection(limit int) eventCollection {
433: 	if limit < 0 {
434: 		limit = 0
435: 	}
436: 	var mem stdruntime.MemStats
437: 	stdruntime.ReadMemStats(&mem)
438: 	return eventCollection{
439: 		events:       make([]Event, 0, limit),
440: 		limit:        limit,
441: 		seenSessions: map[string]bool{},
442: 		memory: MemoryStats{
443: 			StartAllocBytes: mem.Alloc,
444: 			PeakAllocBytes:  mem.Alloc,
445: 			Samples:         1,
446: 		},
447: 	}
448: }
449: 
450: func (c *eventCollection) add(event Event) {
451: 	c.total++
452: 	if event.SessionID != "" && !c.seenSessions[event.SessionID] {
453: 		c.seenSessions[event.SessionID] = true
454: 		c.sessionIDs = append(c.sessionIDs, event.SessionID)
455: 	}
456: 	if c.total == 1 || c.total%64 == 0 {
457: 		c.sampleMemory()
458: 	}
459: 	if c.limit == 0 {
460: 		c.dropped++
461: 		return
462: 	}
463: 	if len(c.events) < c.limit {
464: 		c.events = append(c.events, event)
465: 		return
466: 	}
467: 	copy(c.events, c.events[1:])
468: 	c.events[len(c.events)-1] = event
469: 	c.dropped++
470: }
471: 
472: func (c *eventCollection) captureTerminalOutput(payload map[string]any) {
473: 	if value := terminalOutputValue(payload, 0); value != "" {
474: 		c.terminalOutput = truncateString(value, maxMappedTerminalOutputBytes)
475: 	}
476: }
477: 
478: func terminalOutputValue(value any, depth int) string {
479: 	if depth > 4 {
480: 		return ""
481: 	}
482: 	switch typed := value.(type) {
483: 	case map[string]any:
484: 		for _, key := range []string{"structured_output", "output", "content", "text", "message", "part"} {
485: 			if nested, ok := typed[key]; ok {
486: 				if result := terminalOutputValue(nested, depth+1); result != "" {
487: 					return result
488: 				}
489: 			}
490: 		}
491: 	case []any:
492: 		for i := len(typed) - 1; i >= 0; i-- {
493: 			if result := terminalOutputValue(typed[i], depth+1); result != "" {
494: 				return result
495: 			}
496: 		}
497: 	case string:
498: 		return typed
499: 	}
500: 	return ""
501: }
502: 
503: func (c *eventCollection) finish() {
504: 	c.sampleMemory()
505: }
506: 
507: func (c *eventCollection) sampleMemory() {
508: 	var mem stdruntime.MemStats
509: 	stdruntime.ReadMemStats(&mem)
510: 	c.memory.Samples++
511: 	c.memory.EndAllocBytes = mem.Alloc
512: 	if mem.Alloc > c.memory.PeakAllocBytes {
513: 		c.memory.PeakAllocBytes = mem.Alloc
514: 	}
515: }

522: 		Limit:    c.limit,
523: 	}
524: }

562: func toAgentwrapRequest(req Request) (agentwrap.RunRequest, error) {
563: 	health, err := mapHealthIDs(req.RequireHealth)
564: 	if err != nil {
565: 		return agentwrap.RunRequest{}, err
566: 	}
567: 	caps, err := mapCapabilitiesIDs(req.RequireCaps)
568: 	if err != nil {
569: 		return agentwrap.RunRequest{}, err
570: 	}
571: 	policy, err := mapPermissionPolicy(req.Policy)
572: 	if err != nil {
573: 		return agentwrap.RunRequest{}, err
574: 	}
575: 	metadata := cloneStringMap(req.Metadata)
576: 	if req.RuntimeStorePath != "" {
577: 		if metadata == nil {
578: 			metadata = map[string]string{}
579: 		}
580: 		metadata[agentwrapopencode.MetadataDatabasePath] = req.RuntimeStorePath
581: 		metadata["runtime_store_owner"] = req.RuntimeStoreOwner
582: 	}
583: 	if req.Cache.Key != "" {
584: 		if metadata == nil {
585: 			metadata = map[string]string{}
586: 		}
587: 		cohort, _ := json.Marshal(struct {
588: 			Foundation, Provider, Model, WorkDir, Sandbox, Permissions string
589: 			Policy                                                     PermissionPolicy
590: 		}{req.Cache.Key, req.Provider, req.Model, req.WorkDir, req.Sandbox, req.Permissions, req.Policy})
591: 		sum := sha256.Sum256(cohort)
592: 		metadata["prompt_cache_foundation_key"] = req.Cache.Key
593: 		metadata["prompt_cache_key"] = "ultraplan-cohort-v1-" + hex.EncodeToString(sum[:16])
594: 		metadata["prompt_cache_breakpoint_bytes"] = fmt.Sprintf("%d", req.Cache.BreakpointBytes)
595: 		metadata["prompt_cache_prefix_sha256"] = req.Cache.PrefixDigest
596: 		metadata["prompt_cache_mode"] = req.Cache.Mode
597: 	}
598: 	return agentwrap.RunRequest{
599: 		Prompt:           req.Prompt,
600: 		WorkDir:          req.WorkDir,
601: 		SessionID:        agentwrap.SessionID(req.SessionID),
602: 		SessionAction:    agentwrap.SessionAction(req.SessionAction),
603: 		Provider:         agentwrap.ProviderID(req.Provider),
604: 		Model:            agentwrap.ModelID(req.Model),
605: 		Timeout:          req.Timeout,
606: 		Metadata:         metadata,
607: 		RequireHealth:    health,
608: 		RequireCaps:      caps,
609: 		Sandbox:          agentwrap.SandboxMode(req.Sandbox),
610: 		Permissions:      agentwrap.PermissionMode(req.Permissions),
611: 		PermissionPolicy: policy,
612: 		Validation:       req.Validation,
613: 	}, nil
614: }

643: func mapEvent(event agentwrap.Event) Event {
644: 	rawPresent := event.Raw != nil
645: 	rawSafe := rawPresent && event.Raw.Safe
646: 	payload := cloneAnyMap(event.Payload)
647: 	if runtimeContext, ok := event.Payload["context"].(agentwrap.RuntimeContext); ok {
648: 		payload["provider"] = string(runtimeContext.Provider)
649: 		payload["model"] = string(runtimeContext.Model)
650: 		payload["harness"] = string(runtimeContext.RuntimeKind)
651: 	}
652: 	promoteObservablePayloadFields(payload)
653: 	return Event{
654: 		ID:                string(event.ID),
655: 		RunID:             string(event.RunID),
656: 		SessionID:         string(event.SessionID),
657: 		Time:              event.Time,
658: 		Type:              event.Type,
659: 		Kind:              string(event.Kind()),
660: 		Payload:           payload,
661: 		RawPresent:        rawPresent,
662: 		RawSafe:           rawSafe,
663: 		RawOmitted:        rawPresent,
664: 		RawOmissionReason: rawOmissionReason(rawPresent, rawSafe),
665: 		RawSource:         rawSource(event.Raw),
666: 		RawEncoding:       rawEncoding(event.Raw),
667: 	}
668: }

670: // promoteObservablePayloadFields lifts nested runtime facts (tool names, titles,
671: // text deltas, statuses) to the payload top level so downstream consumers —
672: // run-loop progress summaries, durable run journals, and the web timeline — can
673: // read them without depending on adapter-specific nesting. Existing top-level
674: // values always win.
675: func promoteObservablePayloadFields(payload map[string]any) {
676: 	if len(payload) == 0 {
677: 		return
678: 	}
679: 	for _, key := range []string{"tool", "name", "title", "detail", "text", "delta", "output", "message", "state", "status", "action", "phase"} {
680: 		if value, ok := payload[key].(string); ok && strings.TrimSpace(value) != "" {
681: 			continue
682: 		}
683: 		if found := findNestedPayloadString(payload, key, 0); found != "" {
684: 			payload[key] = found
685: 		}
686: 	}
687: }
688: 
689: func findNestedPayloadString(value any, want string, depth int) string {
690: 	if depth > 4 {
691: 		return ""
692: 	}
693: 	switch typed := value.(type) {
694: 	case map[string]any:
695: 		if s, ok := typed[want].(string); ok && strings.TrimSpace(s) != "" {
696: 			return s
697: 		}
698: 		// Deterministic traversal for stable results across map orders.
699: 		keys := make([]string, 0, len(typed))
700: 		for k := range typed {
701: 			keys = append(keys, k)
702: 		}
703: 		sort.Strings(keys)
704: 		for _, k := range keys {
705: 			if found := findNestedPayloadString(typed[k], want, depth+1); found != "" {
706: 				return found
707: 			}
708: 		}
709: 	case []any:
710: 		for _, item := range typed {
711: 			if found := findNestedPayloadString(item, want, depth+1); found != "" {
712: 				return found

689: func findNestedPayloadString(value any, want string, depth int) string {
690: 	if depth > 4 {
691: 		return ""

696: 			return s
697: 		}

699: 		keys := make([]string, 0, len(typed))
700: 		for k := range typed {
701: 			keys = append(keys, k)
702: 		}
703: 		sort.Strings(keys)
704: 		for _, k := range keys {
705: 			if found := findNestedPayloadString(typed[k], want, depth+1); found != "" {
706: 				return found
707: 			}
708: 		}
709: 	case []any:
710: 		for _, item := range typed {
711: 			if found := findNestedPayloadString(item, want, depth+1); found != "" {

713: 			}
714: 		}
715: 	}

reasoning_details.text:
Very interesting findings from runtime.go:

1. **Event retention limit: `retainedRuntimeEventLimit = 200`** — events beyond 200 DROP OLDEST (`copy(c.events, c.events[1:])`). The review extraction fallback scans `r.Events` in reverse for the result. If the run has >200 events (a reviewer that reads many files generates many tool events!), the FINAL assistant text event IS retained (last 200 kept — the newest kept). Reverse scan finds newest first. OK.

But `reviewOutputCapture.observe` — capture happens in req.OnEvent wrapper, which receives ALL mapped events live (not limited) — last structured payload wins. Fine.

2. **`captureTerminalOutput`**: `terminalOutputValue(payload, 0)` walks keys ["structured_output","output","content","text","message","part"] and takes ANY string found — INCLUDING TOOL OUTPUT payloads! `c.terminalOutput` is OVERWRITTEN by every matching event (`if value != "" { c.terminalOutput = truncateString(value...) }`). So TerminalOutput of the mapped Result (when agentwrap's own TerminalOutput is empty) becomes THE LAST event payload string among those keys — which could be a TOOL RESULT (file content!) rather than the final assistant message!

Wait — order: events processed sequentially; last write wins. Final assistant message is typically the LAST event. But is it? After the assistant's final text, are there other events (e.g., session idle, step finish, usage events)? Those wouldn't carry text keys. Tool results come BEFORE final assistant text in a turn sequence... unless multi-turn: assistant emits result JSON mid-run then does more tool calls? Repair prompt says "do not perform more tool calls".

Hmm, but here's the sharper issue: **the file content read by the reviewer via the read tool flows through an event payload with key "text"/"output"/"content"** (opencode part events for tool parts contain the tool output). If the FINAL event carrying any of those keys is a TOOL RESULT (not assistant text), terminalOutput = poisoned file content. When would the final such event be a tool result? Sequence: ...assistant(final JSON) → [no more]. Assistant text is last. UNLESS the model emits its JSON as part of a tool call or the adapter emits the assistant text event BEFORE some other text-bearing event.

Actually wait — there's a much more direct concern. In opencode, the assistant's final message text arrives as a `message.part.updated` event with part.type=="text". Tool outputs arrive as parts of type "tool" with state.output. Both map into payload keys "text"/"output"/"part" etc. The LAST text-bearing event should be the final assistant message. So terminalOutput usually correct.

BUT what about `extractReviewValue` scanning EVENTS REVERSED with nested keys ["review_result","structured_output","output","content","text","message","part"]? Same reasoning — reversed scan hits the final assistant text first. OK by ordering.

The REAL exposure I flagged (injection via captured tool output overriding a genuine earlier assistant result) requires a text-bearing event AFTER the genuine result. Possible when:
- Model makes a tool call AFTER printing its JSON (models do this despite instructions).
- Multi-attempt repair runs append events to same Result? Each StartRun separate.
- Session continuation events?

383: 	failedContinue := err != nil && repairReq.SessionAction == SessionActionContinue && r.spec.Repair.FreshSessionFallbackOnError && freshRepairFallbackAllowed(firstSDKError(result.Err, err))
384: 	if unsupportedContinue || failedContinue {
385: 		if r.spec.Repair.AllowFreshSessionFallback {
386: 			fallbackReq := repairReq
387: 			fallbackReq.SessionAction = SessionActionFresh
388: 			fallbackReq.SessionID = ""
389: 			result, err = r.startAndWait(fallbackReq)
390: 			summary = repairSummary(repairCtx.Attempt, r.id, fallbackReq, started, result)
391: 			summary.UnsupportedSession = unsupportedContinue
392: 			if unsupportedContinue {
393: 				summary.PolicyDecisionReason = "fresh session fallback after unsupported same-session repair"
394: 			} else {
395: 				summary.PolicyDecisionReason = "fresh session fallback after failed same-session repair"
396: 			}
397: 		} else {
398: 			if unsupportedContinue {
399: 				summary.UnsupportedSession = true
400: 				unsupportedErr := NewError(ErrorRepairExhausted, "validation repair", "same-session repair is unsupported", nil, WithDebugDetail(result.Metadata.Session.UnsupportedReason))
401: 				err = unsupportedErr
402: 				result.Err = unsupportedErr
403: 				result.Status = StatusFailed
404: 				summary.Status = StatusFailed
405: 				summary.Error = unsupportedErr
406: 				summary.ErrorCategory = unsupportedErr.Category
407: 			}
408: 		}
409: 	}
410: 	if err != nil {
411: 		sdkErr := firstSDKError(result.Err, err)
412: 		r.sendEvent(Event{RunID: r.id, SessionID: result.SessionID, Type: "repair.failed", Payload: EventPayloadWithKind(EventValidation, EventPayload{"attempt": repairCtx.Attempt, "error_category": string(sdkErr.Category)})})
413: 		return result, summary, sdkErr
414: 	}
415: 	r.sendEvent(Event{RunID: r.id, SessionID: result.SessionID, Type: "repair.completed", Payload: EventPayloadWithKind(EventValidation, EventPayload{"attempt": repairCtx.Attempt})})
416: 	return result, summary, nil
417: }

419: func freshRepairFallbackAllowed(err *SDKError) bool {
420: 	if err == nil {
421: 		return false
422: 	}
423: 	switch err.Category {
424: 	case ErrorCancellation, ErrorTimeout, ErrorPermission:
425: 		return false
426: 	default:
427: 		return true
428: 	}
429: }

431: func repairSummary(attempt int, parent RunID, req RunRequest, started time.Time, result RunResult) RepairAttemptSummary {

433: 		Attempt:            attempt,
434: 		RunID:              result.RunID,
435: 		ParentRunID:        parent,
436: 		Request:            attemptRequest(req),
437: 		Status:             result.Status,
438: 		StartedAt:          firstTime(result.StartedAt, started),
439: 		FinishedAt:         firstTime(result.FinishedAt, time.Now().UTC()),
440: 		Session:            result.Metadata.Session,
441: 		Permissions:        result.Metadata.Permissions,
442: 		Error:              result.Err,
443: 		PermissionPolicyID: permissionPolicyID(req.PermissionPolicy),
444: 	}
445: 	summary.Duration = summary.FinishedAt.Sub(summary.StartedAt)
446: 	if result.Err != nil {
447: 		summary.ErrorCategory = result.Err.Category
448: 	}
449: 	return summary
450: }

530: // ValidateRun evaluates the configured validators against a completed result.
531: func ValidateRun(ctx context.Context, req RunRequest, result RunResult, spec ValidationSpec) ValidationResult {
532: 	vctx := ValidationContext{Request: req, Result: result, WorkDir: req.WorkDir}
533: 	checks := []ValidationCheck{}
534: 	for _, expectation := range spec.Expectations {
535: 		checks = append(checks, validateExpectation(ctx, vctx, expectation))
536: 	}
537: 	for _, validator := range spec.Validators {
538: 		if validator == nil {
539: 			continue
540: 		}
541: 		checks = append(checks, normalizeCheck(validator.Validate(ctx, vctx)))
542: 	}
543: 	return aggregateValidation(checks)
544: }
545: 
546: func validateExpectation(ctx context.Context, vctx ValidationContext, exp ValidationExpectation) ValidationCheck {
547: 	if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
548: 		return failedCheck(exp, "context active", err.Error(), "validation cancelled")
549: 	}
550: 	switch exp.Kind {
551: 	case ExpectationFile:
552: 		return validatePath(exp, vctx.WorkDir, false)
553: 	case ExpectationDirectory:
554: 		return validatePath(exp, vctx.WorkDir, true)
555: 	case ExpectationArtifact:
556: 		return validateArtifact(exp, vctx.Result)
557: 	case ExpectationMarkdownTemplate:
558: 		return validateMarkdownTemplate(exp, vctx.WorkDir)
559: 	case ExpectationJSON:
560: 		return validateJSON(exp, vctx.WorkDir)
561: 	case ExpectationMetadata:
562: 		return validateMetadata(exp, vctx.Result)
563: 	default:
564: 		return failedCheck(exp, "supported expectation kind", string(exp.Kind), "unknown validation expectation kind")
565: 	}
566: }

568: func validatePath(exp ValidationExpectation, workDir string, wantDir bool) ValidationCheck {
569: 	path := resolvePath(workDir, exp.Path)
570: 	info, err := os.Stat(path)
571: 	if err != nil {
572: 		return failedCheck(exp, path, "missing", "path was not found")
573: 	}
574: 	if wantDir && !info.IsDir() {
575: 		return failedCheck(exp, "directory", "file", "path exists but is not a directory")
576: 	}
577: 	if !wantDir && info.IsDir() {
578: 		return failedCheck(exp, "file", "directory", "path exists but is a directory")
579: 	}
580: 	return passedCheck(exp, path, "present")
581: }

583: func validateArtifact(exp ValidationExpectation, result RunResult) ValidationCheck {
584: 	artifacts := append([]ArtifactRef{}, result.Artifacts...)
585: 	artifacts = append(artifacts, result.Metadata.Artifacts...)
586: 	for _, artifact := range artifacts {
587: 		if exp.ArtifactID != "" && artifact.ID == exp.ArtifactID {
588: 			return passedCheck(exp, string(exp.ArtifactID), "referenced")
589: 		}
590: 		if exp.ArtifactURI != "" && artifact.URI == exp.ArtifactURI {
591: 			return passedCheck(exp, exp.ArtifactURI, "referenced")
592: 		}
593: 	}
594: 	expected := "artifact reference"
595: 	if exp.ArtifactID != "" {
596: 		expected = string(exp.ArtifactID)
597: 	} else if exp.ArtifactURI != "" {
598: 		expected = exp.ArtifactURI
599: 	}
600: 	return failedCheck(exp, expected, "missing", "artifact reference was not present")
601: }

603: func validateMarkdownTemplate(exp ValidationExpectation, workDir string) ValidationCheck {
604: 	templatePath := resolvePath(workDir, exp.TemplatePath)
605: 	artifactPath := resolvePath(workDir, exp.Path)
606: 	templateBytes, err := os.ReadFile(templatePath)
607: 	if err != nil {
608: 		return failedCheck(exp, templatePath, "unreadable", "template file could not be read")
609: 	}
610: 	artifactBytes, err := os.ReadFile(artifactPath)
611: 	if err != nil {
612: 		return failedCheck(exp, artifactPath, "unreadable", "markdown artifact could not be read")
613: 	}
614: 	expectedHeadings := markdownHeadings(string(templateBytes))
615: 	observedHeadings := markdownHeadings(string(artifactBytes))
616: 	if len(expectedHeadings) == 0 {
617: 		return failedCheck(exp, "template headings", "none", "template has no Markdown headings")
618: 	}
619: 	if missing := missingInOrder(expectedHeadings, observedHeadings); len(missing) > 0 {
620: 		return failedCheck(exp, strings.Join(expectedHeadings, " > "), "missing or out of order: "+strings.Join(missing, ", "), "required Markdown headings are missing or out of order")
621: 	}
622: 	if unresolved := unresolvedTemplateSlots(string(artifactBytes)); len(unresolved) > 0 {
623: 		return failedCheck(exp, "resolved template placeholders", strings.Join(unresolved, ", "), "markdown artifact contains unresolved template placeholders")
624: 	}
625: 	return passedCheck(exp, templatePath, "markdown template matched")
626: }

628: func validateJSON(exp ValidationExpectation, workDir string) ValidationCheck {
629: 	path := resolvePath(workDir, exp.Path)
630: 	data, err := os.ReadFile(path)
631: 	if err != nil {
632: 		return failedCheck(exp, path, "unreadable", "JSON file could not be read")
633: 	}
634: 	var value any
635: 	if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &value); err != nil {
636: 		return failedCheck(exp, "well-formed JSON", "invalid JSON", err.Error())
637: 	}
638: 	if len(exp.RequiredFields) > 0 {
639: 		obj, ok := value.(map[string]any)
640: 		if !ok {
641: 			return failedCheck(exp, "JSON object", fmt.Sprintf("%T", value), "required fields need a JSON object")
642: 		}
643: 		missing := []string{}
644: 		for _, field := range exp.RequiredFields {
645: 			if _, ok := obj[field]; !ok {
646: 				missing = append(missing, field)
647: 			}
648: 		}
649: 		if len(missing) > 0 {
650: 			sort.Strings(missing)
651: 			return failedCheck(exp, "required fields: "+strings.Join(exp.RequiredFields, ", "), "missing: "+strings.Join(missing, ", "), "JSON object is missing required fields")
652: 		}
653: 	}
654: 	return passedCheck(exp, path, "valid JSON")
655: }

657: func validateMetadata(exp ValidationExpectation, result RunResult) ValidationCheck {
658: 	if exp.MetadataKey == "" {
659: 		return failedCheck(exp, "metadata key", "empty", "metadata expectation requires a key")
660: 	}
661: 	if result.Metadata.NativeMetadata != nil {
662: 		if _, ok := result.Metadata.NativeMetadata[exp.MetadataKey]; ok {
663: 			return passedCheck(exp, exp.MetadataKey, "present")
664: 		}
665: 	}
666: 	return failedCheck(exp, exp.MetadataKey, "missing", "metadata key was not present")
667: }

669: func aggregateValidation(checks []ValidationCheck) ValidationResult {
670: 	result := ValidationResult{Passed: true, Checks: checks}
671: 	for _, check := range checks {
672: 		check = normalizeCheck(check)
673: 		if check.Skipped {
674: 			result.SkippedCount++
675: 			continue
676: 		}
677: 		if check.Passed {
678: 			result.PassedCount++
679: 			continue
680: 		}
681: 		if severityRequired(check.Severity) {
682: 			result.Passed = false
683: 			result.FailedCount++
684: 			result.Failures = append(result.Failures, ValidationFailure{
685: 				ExpectationID: check.ExpectationID,
686: 				Kind:          check.Kind,
687: 				Severity:      check.Severity,
688: 				Expected:      check.Expected,
689: 				Observed:      check.Observed,
690: 				Detail:        check.Detail,
691: 				RepairHint:    check.RepairHint,
692: 			})
693: 		} else {
694: 			result.SkippedCount++
695: 		}
696: 	}
697: 	if len(checks) == 0 {
698: 		result.Skipped = true
699: 		result.SkippedCount = 1
700: 	}
701: 	if !result.Passed {
702: 		result.Errors = []SDKError{*validationError(result)}
703: 	}
704: 	return result
705: }

707: func repairRequest(req RunRequest, config RepairConfig, repairCtx RepairContext) RunRequest {

712: 	} else {

714: 	}
715: 	if next.SessionID == "" {
716: 		next.SessionID = repairCtx.CurrentResult.SessionID
717: 	}
718: 	next.Prompt = defaultRepairPrompt(repairCtx)
719: 	if config.BuildPrompt != nil {
720: 		next.Prompt = config.BuildPrompt(repairCtx)
721: 	}
722: 	if config.OverrideRequest != nil {
723: 		next = config.OverrideRequest(repairCtx, next)
724: 	}
725: 	return next

728: func defaultRepairPrompt(ctx RepairContext) string {
729: 	var b strings.Builder
730: 	b.WriteString("Repair the previous run output so it satisfies these validation failures. Preserve the existing task intent and update durable artifacts instead of relying on terminal output.\n")
731: 	for _, failure := range ctx.Validation.Failures {
732: 		b.WriteString("\n- ")
733: 		b.WriteString(failure.ExpectationID)
734: 		b.WriteString(": expected ")
735: 		b.WriteString(failure.Expected)
736: 		b.WriteString("; observed ")
737: 		b.WriteString(failure.Observed)
738: 		if failure.RepairHint != "" {
739: 			b.WriteString("; hint ")
740: 			b.WriteString(failure.RepairHint)
741: 		}
742: 	}
743: 	return b.String()
744: }

746: func withValidationMetadata(result RunResult, spec ValidationSpec, history []ValidationResult, repairs []RepairAttemptSummary) RunResult {
747: 	result.Metadata.Validation = ValidationMetadata{
748: 		Configured: len(spec.Expectations) > 0 || len(spec.Validators) > 0,
749: 		History:    append([]ValidationResult(nil), history...),
750: 	}
751: 	if len(history) > 0 {
752: 		result.Metadata.Validation.Final = history[len(history)-1]
753: 	}
754: 	result.Metadata.Repair = RepairMetadata{
755: 		Configured:  spec.Repair.MaxAttempts > 0,
756: 		Attempted:   len(repairs) > 0,
757: 		MaxAttempts: spec.Repair.MaxAttempts,
758: 		Attempts:    append([]RepairAttemptSummary(nil), repairs...),
759: 	}
760: 	for _, repair := range repairs {
761: 		if result.Metadata.Repair.PermissionPolicyID == "" {
762: 			result.Metadata.Repair.PermissionPolicyID = repair.PermissionPolicyID
763: 		}
764: 		if repair.ErrorCategory == ErrorPermission {
765: 			result.Metadata.Repair.PermissionDenied = true
766: 		}
767: 		if repair.UnsupportedSession {
768: 			result.Metadata.Repair.UnsupportedSameSession = true
769: 		}
770: 	}
771: 	if spec.Repair.MaxAttempts > 0 && len(repairs) >= spec.Repair.MaxAttempts && len(history) > 0 && !history[len(history)-1].Passed {
772: 		result.Metadata.Repair.Exhausted = true
773: 		result.Metadata.Repair.ExhaustedReason = "max repair attempts exhausted"
774: 	}
775: 	return result
776: }

837: func normalizeCheck(check ValidationCheck) ValidationCheck {

888: func markdownHeadings(content string) []string {
889: 	headings := []string{}
890: 	for _, line := range strings.Split(content, "\n") {
891: 		trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(line)
892: 		if !strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, "#") {
893: 			continue
894: 		}
895: 		i := 0
896: 		for i < len(trimmed) && trimmed[i] == '#' {
897: 			i++
898: 		}
899: 		if i == 0 || i >= len(trimmed) || trimmed[i] != ' ' {
900: 			continue
901: 		}
902: 		headings = append(headings, strings.TrimSpace(trimmed[i+1:]))
903: 	}
904: 	return headings
905: }

907: func missingInOrder(expected, observed []string) []string {
908: 	missing := []string{}
909: 	pos := 0
910: 	for _, heading := range expected {
911: 		found := false
912: 		for pos < len(observed) {
913: 			if observed[pos] == heading {
914: 				found = true
915: 				pos++
916: 				break
917: 			}
918: 			pos++
919: 		}
920: 		if !found {
921: 			missing = append(missing, heading)
922: 		}
923: 	}
924: 	return missing
925: }

927: func unresolvedTemplateSlots(content string) []string {
928: 	tokens := []string{}
929: 	for _, marker := range []string{"TODO", "TBD", "{{", "}}", "<!-- REQUIRED"} {
930: 		if strings.Contains(content, marker) {
931: 			tokens = append(tokens, marker)
932: 		}
933: 	}
934: 	return tokens
935: }

937: func safeDetail(value string) string {

939: 	const limit = 240
940: 	if len(value) <= limit {
941: 		return value
942: 	}
943: 	return value[:limit] + "..."
944: }

946: func safeFailurePayload(failures []ValidationFailure) []map[string]string {
947: 	payload := make([]map[string]string, 0, len(failures))
948: 	for _, failure := range failures {
949: 		payload = append(payload, map[string]string{
950: 			"expectation_id": failure.ExpectationID,
951: 			"kind":           string(failure.Kind),
952: 			"expected":       failure.Expected,
953: 			"observed":       failure.Observed,
954: 			"detail":         failure.Detail,
955: 			"repair_hint":    failure.RepairHint,
956: 		})
957: 	}
958: 	return payload
959: }

961: func cloneEventPayload(payload EventPayload) EventPayload {

reasoning_details.text:
Key facts from agentwrap validation.go:

1. **Validation runs on the RunResult of the LAST startAndWait** — the validator receives `vctx.Result` = full RunResult of that attempt (TerminalOutput from opencode adapter = "last bounded assistant output"). So agentwrap validates the final attempt's output.

2. **Repair MaxAttempts semantics**: `shouldRepair`: `if MaxAttempts <= 0 || ctx.Attempt > MaxAttempts return false`. Attempt starts at 1 (repairCtx.Attempt = attempt+1 with attempt starting 0). So repairs happen for Attempt=1,2 → 2 REPAIRS + 1 original = up to 3 runtime calls per coverage when production wrapper active. Test says "TestReviewerGetsOneStructuredOutputRepair (exactly 2 calls per coverage)" and "TestReviewerBlocksAfterStructuredOutputRepairIsExhausted (3 calls per coverage)". OK consistent: original + 2 repairs.

3. **CRITICAL for runReviewer's Configured branch**: after repair exhaustion, `r.finish(result, err)` sets waitErr = ErrorRepairExhausted. So StartRun returns err != nil AND result with Validation.Configured=true, Passed=false, Details from final failures. In runReviewer: `candidate, problems := extractValidatedReviewResult(...)`; if extraction of the FINAL attempt's output yields problems → Configured branch → out.Error set. If somehow problems==0 but validation failed (extraction disagreement)... covered earlier.

4. **Events forwarded across ALL attempts** into one channel — so r.Events contains events from original + repair attempts, PLUS lifecycle events ("validation.started", "repair.started", etc.) with Payload {"phase": "started"} etc.

Now — do any agentwrap lifecycle payloads contain keys like "text"/"output"? EventPayload{"phase": "started"} no. But `sendEvent(event)` forwards INNER runtime events verbatim (r.forwardEvents) — those include opencode part events.

Now let me check the opencode Runtime inside agentwrap: how TerminalOutput is computed ("last bounded assistant output observed") and what event payloads look like (do tool outputs appear as payload text/output?).

part.text: Projector confirmed: `tool_use` events carry deep-nested outputs, and ultraplan's `promoteObservablePayloadFields` lifts them to payload top-level where extraction looks first. Let me now verify how the sprint layer consumes events (kind-filtering?) plus service glue:

reasoning_details.text:
Now the picture is clearer for opencode native events:

- `text`/`reasoning` native types → EventMessage. Payload = record.Data (minus type/timestamp). For opencode's `message.part.updated` events, Data includes `part: {...}`. So payload["part"] = part object; terminalOutputValue finds "part" → nested text? part.text is a string under key "text" — wait terminalOutputValue on map: checks keys ["structured_output","output","content","text","message","part"]; payload has "part" → recurse into part map: part map has keys like id/type/text/... "text" → string. Good — assistant TEXT parts feed TerminalOutput.

- BUT: does a TOOL part event come through as native type "tool_use" → EventTool, NOT EventMessage — so it does NOT feed agentwrap TerminalOutput. 

- However: ultraplan Adapter.captureTerminalOutput runs on EVERY event with the SAME key list including "part"/"output"/"content". A tool_use event payload contains... what exactly? record.Data for tool_use in opencode JSON stream: {type:"tool_use", part:{...}}? or {tool:..., state:{output}}? ToolObservation extraction looks for result/output/content keys anywhere nested. The raw payload retains whatever shape; ultraplan's captureTerminalOutput(payload) walks ["structured_output","output","content","text","message","part"] — if tool payload has "part" (opencode message parts include tool parts! In opencode, tool calls are parts of assistant messages: part.type=="tool", part.state.output) → recurse into part → checks keys in order structured_output/output/content/text/message/part → part.state? Not directly — recursion: part map → key "output"? part doesn't have top-level "output"; part.state.output is nested deeper: part → no direct match except... part has "state" (not in list) → returns "". Hmm depth-first per key list at each level: at part level, tries "structured_output"(no), "output"(no—unless part has output), "content"(no), "text"(tool parts may have no text), "message"(no), "part"(no). Returns "". So tool part payloads may NOT yield output via this walker unless shape differs.

- ultraplan's promoteObservablePayloadFields though: findNestedPayloadString searches ANY nesting depth (≤4) for keys "output","text", etc. and PROMOTES them to payload top level! So a tool_use event whose deep part.state.output contains file content gets payload["output"]="<file content>" promoted (deterministic sorted traversal). THEN:
  - ultraplan captureTerminalOutput sees payload["output"] non-empty → c.terminalOutput = <file content>! Overwritten by every subsequent matching event.
  - extractReviewValue on that payload: whole-map decode fails; then keys: "review_result" no..."output" YES → extractReviewJSON(file content) → any decodable review-result-looking object inside the file content becomes a candidate!

So in the ultraplan-mapped event stream (which is ALL the sprint layer sees — both captured.observe and r.Events scan use mapped events), TOOL OUTPUTS ARE FIRST-CLASS RESULT CANDIDATES via promotion. The only ordering protection: last one wins.

Also note promoteObservablePayloadFields promotes from nested maps sorted-key traversal; "state" contains "output"... findNestedPayloadString(payload,"output"): payload map itself lacks "output" string field → iterate nested sorted: "part" → part map lacks "output"? part.state.output — part map iteration sorted keys: ... "state" → state map has "output" → found! Promoted. Yes.

Wait — but also check: does promoteObservablePayloadFields skip when top-level value already exists as non-empty string ("Existing top-level values always win")? For tool events there's no existing "output" at top. Promoted.

And reasoning events (`reasoning` nativeType) ALSO map to EventMessage — their part.text is REASONING content which feeds appendTerminalOutput TOO! So model reasoning text gets concatenated into TerminalOutput (appendTerminalOutput joins current+next when not prefix/suffix). That means TerminalOutput can contain interleaved reasoning + text chunks — extraction scans whole string for LAST decodable object. Reasoning could echo file content (models often quote code while reasoning!). This strengthens the injection surface: poisoned file content quoted in reasoning/text after the final answer... but ordering still matters.

Actually — here's the cleanest realistic mis-trigger WITHOUT any attacker: **the reviewer reads a governed input or changed file that CONTAINS a JSON example** (e.g., the review protocol doc itself shows the canonical schema example with `"coverageId":"<contract-id>"`, or requirements.md contains JSON snippets, or the handbook documents the schema!). Reviewer reads files AFTER emitting its answer? No—reads happen before answering normally. Last-wins ⇒ genuine answer wins. UNLESS the model emits NO valid answer (prose/refusal/truncation) → then the last tool-output-embedded decodable object wins → could be a schema EXAMPLE from the docs with placeholder coverageId... needs exact coverageId match to validate ("coverageId must be %q"). Schema examples usually have placeholder values like "contract-slug" — mismatch → invalid → repair → blocked. Fail-closed-ish. With crafted content targeting the real coverageId → silent pass.

So the concrete defect: **result attribution ignores event provenance (kind/role); any tool-result or reasoning payload containing a well-formed review JSON for the right coverageId can satisfy validation, turning "reviewer produced no valid result" (should block) into "pass"**. Trigger requires (a) reviewer fails to emit parseable canonical JSON in its final message(s), AND (b) some earlier/later event payload embeds a complete valid object with correct coverageId, AND (c) that object passes citation/schema gates (empty findings trivially pass). Attacker prerequisite: control over any file the reviewer reads (changed target paths — actor-authored during execute — or governed inputs authored by earlier model stages). Given UltraPlan's threat model treats execute-stage artifacts as actor-editable evidence requiring containment checks, an execute-stage prompt-injection or compromised dependency writing into changed files is a plausible source; consequence: governance gate silently bypassed (fail-open where design intends fail-closed).

Counter-evidence to seek:
1. Does the sprint layer filter events by Kind before extraction? (No — extractReviewResult iterates all r.Events; observe() takes all.)
2. Does agentwrap's TerminalOutput (authoritative, DB-backed assistant text) take precedence such that tool outputs never reach extraction? Production path: vctx.Result.TerminalOutput = agentwrap TerminalOutput (assistant text + reasoning concat, DB-reconciled). Validator prefers it. runReviewer's extractValidatedReviewResult prefers r.TerminalOutput too. So injection wins ONLY when assistant-derived TerminalOutput contains NO decodable object. Then fallback: reverse event scan / captured. So the fail-open window == "model didn't emit parseable JSON but SOME payload did".
   - Also mapped.TerminalOutput fallback in runtime.go line 388: `if mapped.TerminalOutput == "" && events.terminalOutput != ""` — events.terminalOutput includes promoted tool outputs! So if agentwrap produced empty TerminalOutput (e.g., older opencode omitting text events — the exact scenario the comment mentions), ultraplan fills it with the LAST promoted text-bearing payload — possibly a TOOL result. Then BOTH validator and local extraction treat tool output as the assistant answer. This is precisely the documented recovery path being widened to non-assistant sources.
3. Is there a test pinning kind-awareness? Check review_test.go extraction tests — they use part.text payloads (assistant-shaped). No tool-shaped test likely.

This is Finding #1 (high severity, high confidence in mechanism; likelihood moderate).

Next, I noticed in runtime.go StartRun: on ctx.Done + 5s timeout path, returns mapped WITHOUT draining eventsCh — goroutine leak bounded. Minor.

Another observation: `retainedRuntimeEventLimit = 200` — with dropped events, r.Events holds last 200. Reverse scan fine.

Now — the OTHER major thing to scrutinize: **appendTerminalOutput concatenation**: TerminalOutput = reasoning+text CONCATENATED across all message parts of the session. If the model streams multiple text parts (e.g., intermediate commentary + final JSON), the concatenation contains MULTIPLE objects; extraction takes the LAST decodable — typically the final. But consider resume/continue sessions: same session, new turn appended — TerminalOutput accumulates across turns within ONE startAndWait? Each StartRun spawns new opencode process reading session history? Does continuation replay prior messages as events? If continuing a session re-emits previous message parts as events (opencode might stream only new activity), fine.

Hmm, also `strings.HasPrefix(next, current)` dedupe logic suggests streaming deltas re-sends.

OK. Next steps: read the remaining sprint service glue: startSprintRuntime, deleteCompletedSession, runtimeRequest, acquireMutationContext, prepareSharedPromptContext persistCache, syncDir, hashFile/mustArtifactPath, inside(). Also review_test.go. Also sprint_commands.go exit mapping. Let me batch.

reasoning_details.text:
Store lifecycle confirmed. Now the deleteSessions mismatch is solid: - Review runs write sessions into scoped stores (`OPENCODE_DB` env from metadata). - On success, review calls `deleteCompletedSession(sessionID)` → `Adapter.DeleteSession` → `deleteSessions` closure → SQL against GLOBAL db (no OPENCODE_DB) + `opencode session delete ` (global) + checkpoint/VACUUM global. - The scoped store's data survives; only the 72h/2GiB sweep reclaims it. Observable bad outcome: after every successful review, per-coverage SQLite stores under `projects/

/sprints//.ultraplan/runtime/opencode//opencode.db` retain full reviewer transcripts (each includes the entire embedded prompt with governed inputs — potentially MBs each). With daily reviews and several coverages, disk grows unboundedly between sweeps (72h age OR aggregate 2GiB quota — quota is per-sprint scope total >2GiB, so up to 2GiB per sprint can accumulate!). Also every successful review executes a pointless `DELETE FROM event_sequence` + possible VACUUM/checkpoint churn against the shared global DB (if `opencode session delete` succeeds on missing id — need to check; if it errors, no vacuum happens but deletes still fail silently). 100: func (r *concurrentReviewRuntime) StartRun(_ context.Context, req pruntime.Request) (pruntime.Result, error) {
101: 	n := r.active.Add(1)
102: 	for {
103: 		old := r.max.Load()
104: 		if n <= old || r.max.CompareAndSwap(old, n) {
105: 			break

108: 	time.Sleep(5 * time.Millisecond)
109: 	r.active.Add(-1)

display.text:
# Review Sprint Protocol

> Role: post-implementation sprint review orchestrator.
> Canonical output: `projects/<project>/sprints/<sprint>/review.md`.
> Contract and protocol paths are resolved dynamically from project and sprint indexes.

This protocol replaces the older manually coordinated review. It reviews the implemented sprint scope against selected contracts, technical-handbook guidance, sprint decisions, plan tasks, and verification evidence. It does not redesign the sprint, fix product code, mutate tests, change governed inputs, or mutate Git state.

## Purpose And Order

Run review after `execute` and before deep smoke:

```text
execute -> review -> smoke
```

Review runs first because it is cheaper and more deterministic than live smoke. Applicable blocker or high-severity findings stop the default flow before smoke.

## 1. Discover Context

Required identifiers:

```text
Project: <project>
Sprint: <sprint-slug>
Project index: projects/<project>/project-index.md
Sprint directory: projects/<project>/sprints/<sprint-slug>/
Implementation directory: resolved from project-index.md
```

Read `project-index.md`, `requirements.md`, `sprint-index.md`, `technical-handbook.md`, selected `reasoning/*.md`, `reasoning.md`, `plan.md`, `execute.md` when present, `.run-state.json` when present, and `flow-state.json`.

Resolve every selected contract and required review protocol through the project index. Do not maintain a hardcoded contract-name map. Fail preflight for missing, duplicate, unreadable, unknown, or escaping catalog paths.

## 2. Freeze Review Scope

Before reviewer execution, determine and display:

- target implementation root and revision/fingerprint;
- changed paths or explicit full-target scope;

- approved deterministic verification commands;

## 3. Run Deterministic Checks

Check decision conformance, plan/execute evidence, approved verification commands, reviewer coverage, evidence containment, citation validity, deviations/deferred scope, and prohibited mutations. Never execute arbitrary shell text extracted from generated Markdown; approved commands run as explicit executable/argument arrays.

## 4. Run Independent Reviewers

UltraPlan owns bounded fan-out and does not assume a reviewer runtime can spawn subagents. Run one structured reviewer per selected contract and one for the technical handbook.

Each reviewer classifies applicability as `direct`, `partial`, `not_triggered`, or `explicitly_deferred`; reports conformance, severity, contained evidence, issue, and recommended action; and returns schema-versioned structured data without writing files. Missing, malformed, duplicate, or failed mandatory reviewer results remain failures and are never silently dropped.

Structured-result repair is bounded: first repair in the retained session when possible, then make at most one fresh-session fallback. Persist only schema- and citation-valid checkpoints, resume compatible completed coverage by default, and reserve a full restart for an explicitly incompatible schema, model, or input fingerprint.

Collect all available results even when one fails. Write sections for Review Context, Input Fingerprint And Scope, Decision Conformance, Plan Execution, Verification Evidence, Contract Conformance, Technical Handbook Conformance, Applicability And Deferred Scope, Findings, Deviations, and Final Assessment.

Product code computes the verdict:

- `pass`: all mandatory work completed; no applicable blocker/high finding;
- `pass_with_findings`: all mandatory work completed; only medium/low/info findings;
- `fail`: blocker/high finding, failed required verification, invalid evidence, or missing mandatory reviewer;
- `blocked`: required inputs, scope, runtime/model, or verification environment unavailable.

An LLM may summarize but cannot choose or override the verdict.

## 6. Validate And Replace

Validate required sections, selected-contract/handbook coverage, failed-reviewer disclosure, contained citations, severity/verdict consistency, fingerprint/scope, redaction, and absence of smoke claims. Write atomically. A failed/cancelled run must not corrupt the last complete artifact. A successful explicitly started review may replace an older manual or generated `review.md`.

The TUI exposes the same typed review use case as the CLI: readiness, dry-run, prompt preview, confirmation, scope/contracts, progress, cancellation, findings, verdict, rerun, recovery, and `review.md` preview. It must not call CLI handlers or parse terminal output.

## Stop Conditions

Return `blocked` before execution for missing/invalid inputs, unresolved catalog entries, ambiguous implementation scope, or unavailable review runtime/model. Return `fail`, with a synthesized review where possible, for failed verification, invalid/missing mandatory reviewer evidence, or applicable blocker/high findings.
